experiment: Newton's Rings Wave Interference - Question Bank
description: Comprehensive 50-Question Physics Question Bank for Newton's Rings Wave Interference

questions.question: Why is the central spot in Newton's rings observed to be dark in reflected light?
options: Because reflection at the lower air-to-glass boundary introduces an abrupt π phase reversal (λ/2 path shift)
Because light is completely absorbed by the glass plate at the point of contact
Because the film thickness is equal to a full wavelength at the center
Because the lens curvature reflects all light away from the microscope
questions.answer: Because reflection at the lower air-to-glass boundary introduces an abrupt π phase reversal (λ/2 path shift)
questions.correct_option: Because reflection at the lower air-to-glass boundary introduces an abrupt π phase reversal (λ/2 path shift)
questions.explanation: At the point of contact, film thickness t = 0. Reflection from the denser glass plate introduces a π phase reversal (path difference of λ/2), satisfying the condition for complete destructive interference.

questions.question: In reflected monochromatic light, how does the diameter Dₘ of the m-th dark Newton's ring depend on ring order m?
options: Dₘ is proportional to the square root of m (Dₘ ∝ √m)
Dₘ is directly proportional to m (Dₘ ∝ m)
Dₘ is proportional to m squared (Dₘ ∝ m²)
Dₘ is inversely proportional to m
questions.answer: Dₘ is proportional to the square root of m (Dₘ ∝ √m)
questions.correct_option: Dₘ is proportional to the square root of m (Dₘ ∝ √m)
questions.explanation: From the interference condition 2t = mλ and lens sagitta t = Dₘ² / (8R), we obtain Dₘ² = 4mλR, so Dₘ = 2√(mλR) ∝ √m.

questions.question: Why do Newton's rings crowd closer together as their order m increases?
options: Because ring diameter scales as √m, and the difference between successive square roots decreases with increasing m
Because the wavelength of light decreases towards the edge of the lens
Because optical absorption increases rapidly in thicker air films
Because spherical aberration curves the wavefront into ellipses
questions.answer: Because ring diameter scales as √m, and the difference between successive square roots decreases with increasing m
questions.correct_option: Because ring diameter scales as √m, and the difference between successive square roots decreases with increasing m
questions.explanation: Since Dₘ ∝ √m, the radial spacing between consecutive rings (e.g. √10 - √9 < √2 - √1) continuously decreases, resulting in fringe crowding at larger radii.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the diameters of the (m+p)-th and m-th dark rings in an air film?
questions.answer: Dₘ₊ₚ² − Dₘ² = 4pλR
questions.correct_option: Dₘ₊ₚ² − Dₘ² = 4pλR
questions.explanation: Dₘ₊ₚ² = 4(m+p)λR and Dₘ² = 4mλR. Subtracting the two yields Dₘ₊ₚ² − Dₘ² = 4pλR, eliminating central contact uncertainty.

questions.question: If a liquid of refractive index μ = 1.33 (water) replaces the air film between the lens and glass plate, what happens to the rings?
options: The rings contract inwards because Dₘ ∝ 1/√μ
The rings expand outwards because Dₘ ∝ √μ
The rings disappear completely due to total internal reflection
The central spot transforms into a bright fringe
questions.answer: The rings contract inwards because Dₘ ∝ 1/√μ
questions.correct_option: The rings contract inwards because Dₘ ∝ 1/√μ
questions.explanation: With medium of refractive index μ, the path condition is 2μt = mλ, leading to Dₘ² = 4mλR / μ. Since μ > 1, all ring diameters contract by a factor of 1/√μ.

questions.question: Why is a plano-convex lens with a very large radius of curvature (e.g. R = 100 cm) used instead of a strongly curved lens?
options: To ensure the air film thickness increases very slowly, producing wide rings that can be measured accurately with a travelling microscope
To prevent chromatic dispersion in the glass material
Because small radius lenses cannot reflect monochromatic light
To increase the optical intensity of the central spot
questions.answer: To ensure the air film thickness increases very slowly, producing wide rings that can be measured accurately with a travelling microscope
questions.correct_option: To ensure the air film thickness increases very slowly, producing wide rings that can be measured accurately with a travelling microscope
questions.explanation: A large radius R keeps the film thickness t extremely small over a large radial distance r, producing broad, measurable fringe diameters without excessive crowding.

questions.question: What type of interference fringes are Newton's rings classified as?
questions.answer: Fringes of equal thickness (Fizeau fringes)
questions.correct_option: Fringes of equal thickness (Fizeau fringes)
questions.explanation: Newton's rings are localized fringes of equal thickness because each dark or bright circular fringe corresponds to a locus of constant air film thickness t.

questions.question: What is the expected appearance of the central spot in Newton's rings observed in transmitted light?
options: Bright, because no relative phase shift occurs between the two transmitted rays at t = 0
Dark, identical to the reflected pattern
Completely invisible because transmitted light does not interfere
questions.answer: Bright, because no relative phase shift occurs between the two transmitted rays at t = 0
questions.correct_option: Bright, because no relative phase shift occurs between the two transmitted rays at t = 0
questions.explanation: In transmitted light, both interfering rays either undergo two internal reflections or none, resulting in zero net reflection phase difference at t = 0 (constructive interference).

questions.question: When plotting Dₙ² on the y-axis against ring order n on the x-axis for an air film, what does the slope of the straight line represent?
questions.answer: Slope = 4λR
questions.correct_option: Slope = 4λR
questions.explanation: Since Dₙ² = 4nλR, differentiating with respect to n gives d(Dₙ²)/dn = 4λR. Thus, the linear regression slope is exactly 4λR.

questions.question: In an experiment with Sodium light (λ = 589.3 nm) and R = 100 cm, what is the theoretical diameter of the 4th dark ring in air?
Why do Newton's rings become closer and closer together (crowded) as the ring order n increases away from the center?
options: The air film thickness increases non-linearly with radius as r² (since t = r² / 2R)
The wavelength of light changes with distance
The glass plate becomes thicker at the edges
Light intensity drops to zero at higher orders
questions.answer: The air film thickness increases non-linearly with radius as r² (since t = r² / 2R)
questions.correct_option: The air film thickness increases non-linearly with radius as r² (since t = r² / 2R)
questions.explanation: Because t = r² / (2R), the radial spacing Δr = r_n - r_{n-1} ∝ 1/√n. Consequently, outer fringes become progressively narrower and pack tightly together.

questions.question: What is the theoretical diameter D_n of the n-th dark ring in reflected light for an air film (µ = 1)?
questions.explanation: Condition for dark ring is 2t = nλ. Since t = r_n² / (2R), r_n² = nλR, which gives D_n = 2r_n = 2√(nλR).

questions.question: What is the theoretical diameter D_n of the n-th bright ring in reflected light for an air film?
questions.explanation: Condition for bright ring is 2t = (2n - 1)λ/2. Thus r_n² = (2n - 1)λR / 2, giving D_n = 2r_n = √[2(2n - 1)λR].

questions.question: In the Newton's rings experiment, what fundamental linear relationship eliminates the error caused by imperfect contact at the center (e.g. dust particle)?
options: D_{n+p}² - D_n² = 4 * p * λ * R / µ
questions.answer: D_{n+p}² - D_n² = 4 * p * λ * R / µ
questions.correct_option: D_{n+p}² - D_n² = 4 * p * λ * R / µ
questions.explanation: Any zero-point offset error in film thickness shifts all D² values equally: D_n² = 4nλR + 4cR. Subtracting two squared diameters cancels the constant c completely.

questions.question: How is the refractive index µ of an unknown transparent liquid determined using Newton's rings?
questions.answer: µ = (D_{n+p}² - D_n²)_air / (D_{n+p}² - D_n²)_liquid
questions.correct_option: µ = (D_{n+p}² - D_n²)_air / (D_{n+p}² - D_n²)_liquid
questions.explanation: Since (D_{n+p}² - D_n²) = 4pλR / µ, taking the ratio of the air measurement (µ_air = 1) to the liquid measurement yields the liquid refractive index µ directly.

questions.question: What happens to the diameters of Newton's rings when water (µ = 1.33) is introduced between the lens and the glass plate?
options: All ring diameters contract (become smaller by a factor of 1/√1.33 ≈ 0.867)
The central spot turns bright in reflection
questions.answer: All ring diameters contract (become smaller by a factor of 1/√1.33 ≈ 0.867)
questions.correct_option: All ring diameters contract (become smaller by a factor of 1/√1.33 ≈ 0.867)
questions.explanation: Since D_n ∝ 1/√µ, filling the gap with a denser optical medium reduces effective wavelength, compressing all ring diameters inward.

questions.question: If the radius of curvature R of the plano-convex lens is increased (flatter lens), how do the ring diameters change?
options: Ring diameters increase (fringes expand outward and are easier to measure)
questions.answer: Ring diameters increase (fringes expand outward and are easier to measure)
questions.correct_option: Ring diameters increase (fringes expand outward and are easier to measure)
questions.explanation: Since D_n = 2√(nλR), larger radius of curvature R stretches out the circular fringes radially, enabling higher measurement precision with a travelling microscope.

questions.question: Why is a lens with a very large radius of curvature (e.g. R = 100 cm or 200 cm) preferred in the Newton's rings experiment?
options: To make the air film wedge angle extremely small so the rings have conveniently large diameters
To focus the light into a small point
questions.answer: To make the air film wedge angle extremely small so the rings have conveniently large diameters
questions.correct_option: To make the air film wedge angle extremely small so the rings have conveniently large diameters
questions.explanation: A large R creates an extremely gradual increase in air film thickness, expanding the ring diameters into the millimeter scale readable by a standard vernier microscope.

questions.question: If a speck of dust or grit is trapped at the point of contact between the lens and flat glass plate, what happens to the central spot?
options: The central spot becomes bright instead of dark because the film thickness at the contact is no longer zero
The rings turn into straight lines
The light changes from yellow to green
questions.answer: The central spot becomes bright instead of dark because the film thickness at the contact is no longer zero
questions.correct_option: The central spot becomes bright instead of dark because the film thickness at the contact is no longer zero
questions.explanation: A dust particle maintains a finite air gap t > 0. If 2t + λ/2 = mλ (e.g. t = λ/4), constructive interference occurs, making the center bright.

questions.question: In an experiment with Sodium light (λ = 589.3 nm) and R = 1.0 m, the diameter of the 4th dark ring is 3.07 mm. What is the diameter of the 16th dark ring?
In reflected light, what is the optical path difference between the two interfering rays for a film of thickness t at normal incidence?
questions.explanation: The beam reflecting from the top of the lower glass plate undergoes an internal-to-external reflection at a denser medium, introducing a Stokes phase shift of π (path difference λ/2). Total Δ = 2µt + λ/2.

questions.question: If Newton's rings are viewed in transmitted light, why is the central spot bright?
options: Both interfering rays either undergo two internal reflections or none, resulting in zero net reflection phase change at t = 0
questions.answer: Both interfering rays either undergo two internal reflections or none, resulting in zero net reflection phase change at t = 0
questions.correct_option: Both interfering rays either undergo two internal reflections or none, resulting in zero net reflection phase change at t = 0
questions.explanation: In transmission, ray 1 has no reflection and ray 2 has two internal reflections (each π, total 2π = 0). At t = 0, optical path difference is zero, giving a bright center.

questions.question: How do the ring diameters in transmitted light compare to those in reflected light?
options: The rings are complementary: dark rings in reflected light become bright rings in transmitted light, and vice versa
They are identical in position and intensity
Transmitted rings are twice as large
questions.answer: The rings are complementary: dark rings in reflected light become bright rings in transmitted light, and vice versa
questions.correct_option: The rings are complementary: dark rings in reflected light become bright rings in transmitted light, and vice versa
questions.explanation: By conservation of energy (R + T = 1 for non-absorbing media), constructive interference in reflection corresponds to destructive interference in transmission.

questions.question: Why are Newton's rings circular in shape rather than straight lines?
options: The air film between a spherical lens surface and a plane plate has circular symmetry of equal thickness (t = r² / 2R)
Light rays rotate as they propagate
questions.answer: The air film between a spherical lens surface and a plane plate has circular symmetry of equal thickness (t = r² / 2R)
questions.correct_option: The air film between a spherical lens surface and a plane plate has circular symmetry of equal thickness (t = r² / 2R)
questions.explanation: The loci of points having identical thickness t form concentric circles centered at the point of contact; hence the fringes of equal thickness are concentric circles.

questions.question: If white light is used instead of monochromatic light in Newton's rings, what is observed?
options: A central dark spot surrounded by a few colored concentric rings, fading into uniform white illumination
A solid dark circle covering the lens
questions.answer: A central dark spot surrounded by a few colored concentric rings, fading into uniform white illumination
questions.correct_option: A central dark spot surrounded by a few colored concentric rings, fading into uniform white illumination
questions.explanation: At the center, t = 0 is dark for all wavelengths. For outer rings, each wavelength has its own ring radius r(λ) ∝ √λ; the overlapping colors blur into white beyond a few orders.

questions.question: In a travelling microscope, why is the crosshair always traversed along the horizontal diameter in one consistent direction (e.g. strictly left to right)?
options: To prevent backlash error in the micrometer lead screw
questions.answer: To prevent backlash error in the micrometer lead screw
questions.correct_option: To prevent backlash error in the micrometer lead screw
questions.explanation: Travelling microscopes use precision lead screws; moving only in one direction ensures the gear teeth remain engaged on the same flank, avoiding mechanical backlash error.

questions.question: If D_20² = 25.0 mm² and D_10² = 12.5 mm² for an air film using λ = 500 nm, what is the radius of curvature R of the lens?
If the plano-convex lens is replaced by a convex lens placed on a concave lens of larger radius R2 > R1, what is the effective radius R_eff in the ring formula?
questions.explanation: Thickness t = (r² / 2R1) - (r² / 2R2) = (r² / 2) * (1/R1 - 1/R2). Thus 1/R_eff = 1/R1 - 1/R2.

questions.question: What is the slope of the graph plotted between D_n² (y-axis) and ring order n (x-axis) for an air film?
questions.answer: Slope = 4 * λ * R
questions.correct_option: Slope = 4 * λ * R
questions.explanation: Since D_n² = 4nλR, the linear equation y = m*x has slope m = 4λR. Measuring this slope provides an accurate way to find λ or R.

questions.question: How is the radius of curvature R of the plano-convex lens independently measured in a physics laboratory?
options: Using a spherometer or Boy's optical method
Using a vernier caliper directly across the surface
questions.answer: Using a spherometer or Boy's optical method
questions.correct_option: Using a spherometer or Boy's optical method
questions.explanation: A spherometer measures the sagitta h of the curved spherical surface: R = l² / (6h) + h / 2.

questions.question: What optical instrument is used to measure the fringe ring diameters with 0.01 mm precision?
options: A travelling microscope with a vernier scale
A micrometer screw gauge clamped to the lens
questions.answer: A travelling microscope with a vernier scale
questions.correct_option: A travelling microscope with a vernier scale
questions.explanation: A travelling microscope mounted on horizontal lead screw slides allows crosshairs to align with left and right edges of each ring to measure D_n = |x_right - x_left|.

questions.question: Why is the contrast of Newton's rings observed in reflected light much higher than in transmitted light?
options: In reflection, the two interfering rays have nearly equal amplitudes (~4% each), while in transmission one ray is ~96% and the other ~0.16%
Transmitted light is absorbed by air
The lens reflects 100% of the light
questions.answer: In reflection, the two interfering rays have nearly equal amplitudes (~4% each), while in transmission one ray is ~96% and the other ~0.16%
questions.correct_option: In reflection, the two interfering rays have nearly equal amplitudes (~4% each), while in transmission one ray is ~96% and the other ~0.16%
questions.explanation: At glass-air boundaries, reflection is ~4%. In reflection, both beams have amplitude ~0.2, yielding near-zero minimum. In transmission, beam 1 is ~0.96 and beam 2 is ~0.0016, so the interference modulation is tiny.

questions.question: What happens to Newton's rings if the plano-convex lens is slowly lifted vertically away from the flat glass plate?
options: The rings collapse inward and disappear into the center one by one
The rings turn into vertical straight lines
questions.answer: The rings collapse inward and disappear into the center one by one
questions.correct_option: The rings collapse inward and disappear into the center one by one
questions.explanation: Lifting the lens increases the thickness t everywhere. To maintain a constant thickness for a given order, the radius r must decrease: rings contract inward toward the center.

questions.question: If an air film Newton's ring pattern has D_10 = 5.00 mm, what would its diameter be if the air is replaced by benzene (µ = 1.50)?
What is the thickness of the air film at the position of the 5th dark ring for sodium light (λ = 589.3 nm)?
questions.explanation: Condition for dark ring: 2t = nλ. For n = 5: t = 5 * λ / 2 = 5 * 589.3 nm / 2 = 1473.25 nm ≈ 1.47 µm.

questions.question: What is the thickness of the air film at the position of the 1st bright ring for λ = 589 nm?
questions.explanation: Condition for bright ring: 2t = (2n - 1)λ / 2. For n = 1: 2t = λ/2 -> t = λ / 4 = 589 nm / 4 = 147.25 nm ≈ 0.147 µm.

questions.question: If the flat glass plate underneath is replaced by a plane mirror (reflectance ≈ 100%), why do Newton's rings become faint or invisible in reflected light?
options: The high reflectance of the mirror makes the second beam (~100%) vastly stronger than the first beam (~4%), ruining interference contrast
Metal mirrors absorb all phase shifts
The focal length of the lens becomes zero
questions.answer: The high reflectance of the mirror makes the second beam (~100%) vastly stronger than the first beam (~4%), ruining interference contrast
questions.correct_option: The high reflectance of the mirror makes the second beam (~100%) vastly stronger than the first beam (~4%), ruining interference contrast
questions.explanation: Fringe visibility V = 2√(I1*I2) / (I1 + I2). When I2 >> I1 (100% vs 4%), visibility drops to 2√(0.04) / 1.04 ≈ 0.38 / 1.04 ≈ 0.38, washing out the rings.

questions.question: How does the ring pattern change if a plano-convex lens with a cylindrical surface is used instead of a spherical surface?
options: The fringes become straight, parallel lines running parallel to the cylinder axis
questions.answer: The fringes become straight, parallel lines running parallel to the cylinder axis
questions.correct_option: The fringes become straight, parallel lines running parallel to the cylinder axis
questions.explanation: A cylinder has constant curvature along its generator axis; the air film thickness varies in only one dimension (t = x² / 2R), producing straight parallel fringes.

questions.question: If an optical flat with an elliptical surface is used with a flat plate, what shape do the fringes take?
questions.answer: Concentric ellipses
questions.correct_option: Concentric ellipses
questions.explanation: Lines of constant air film thickness t = (x²/2R_x) + (y²/2R_y) form concentric ellipses.

questions.question: What happens to the Newton's rings if the Sodium lamp source is replaced by an extended Helium-Neon laser (632.8 nm)?
options: The rings are red and hundreds of orders remain visible due to the high coherence length of the laser
questions.answer: The rings are red and hundreds of orders remain visible due to the high coherence length of the laser
questions.correct_option: The rings are red and hundreds of orders remain visible due to the high coherence length of the laser
questions.explanation: Because a laser has an extremely long temporal coherence length (meters vs fractions of a millimeter for sodium), high-contrast rings persist to very high orders.

questions.question: In Newton's rings, why does the 45° glass plate need to be only semi-reflecting (unsilvered)?
options: An unsilvered glass plate reflects ~4-8% downward and transmits ~90% upward, allowing the user to view the fringes clearly
Unsilvered plates rotate light polarization by 90°
questions.answer: An unsilvered glass plate reflects ~4-8% downward and transmits ~90% upward, allowing the user to view the fringes clearly
questions.correct_option: An unsilvered glass plate reflects ~4-8% downward and transmits ~90% upward, allowing the user to view the fringes clearly
questions.explanation: An ordinary clean microscope slide provides adequate reflection to illuminate the film while remaining transparent enough for reflected fringe rays to pass through to the eyepiece.

questions.question: What is the effect on the ring pattern if the plano-convex lens has a slight wedge angle relative to the plate?
options: The circular rings become distorted into eccentric or shifted non-concentric curves
The rings turn into a single point
The rings change color to blue
questions.answer: The circular rings become distorted into eccentric or shifted non-concentric curves
questions.correct_option: The circular rings become distorted into eccentric or shifted non-concentric curves
questions.explanation: Superimposing a linear wedge gradient on a quadratic spherical curvature shifts the centers of the rings and distorts circular symmetry into eccentric circles.

questions.question: If two wavelengths λ1 = 589.0 nm and λ2 = 589.6 nm (the Sodium D-doublet) illuminate Newton's rings, what happens at very high orders?
options: Periodic fading and revival (beating) of fringe visibility occurs where bright rings of λ1 coincide with dark rings of λ2
The rings permanently disappear at order 2
questions.answer: Periodic fading and revival (beating) of fringe visibility occurs where bright rings of λ1 coincide with dark rings of λ2
questions.correct_option: Periodic fading and revival (beating) of fringe visibility occurs where bright rings of λ1 coincide with dark rings of λ2
questions.explanation: Because of the slight difference in wavelength (Δλ = 0.6 nm), the two ring patterns drift in and out of phase, creating visibility beats every n ≈ λ / (2Δλ) ≈ 490 orders.

questions.question: If the radius of the 10th dark ring is r_10 = 2.45 mm for λ = 600 nm, what is the radius of curvature R of the lens?
What is the area enclosed between the n-th and (n+1)-th dark rings in an air film?
options: Area = π * λ * R (constant for all orders n)
questions.answer: Area = π * λ * R (constant for all orders n)
questions.correct_option: Area = π * λ * R (constant for all orders n)
questions.explanation: A_n = π r_n² = π(nλR). The incremental area between consecutive rings is A_{n+1} - A_n = π(n+1)λR - πnλR = πλR, which is constant across all rings.

questions.question: Why does the central spot in Newton's rings appear slightly grey rather than pitch black in real laboratory conditions?
options: Microscopic surface roughness and slight contamination prevent perfect zero thickness over the contact area
Glass reflects 50% of light at normal incidence
questions.answer: Microscopic surface roughness and slight contamination prevent perfect zero thickness over the contact area
questions.correct_option: Microscopic surface roughness and slight contamination prevent perfect zero thickness over the contact area
questions.explanation: Real glass surfaces have sub-nanometer surface asperities and dust films, preventing ideal zero-gap contact across the entire central zone.

questions.question: If the lens is made of crown glass (µ_lens = 1.52), the liquid has µ_liq = 1.65, and the flat plate is flint glass (µ_plate = 1.70), what is the central spot in reflected light?
options: Dark, because both reflections occur at denser media (π phase shift at each surface, net relative phase shift = 0, but Δ = 0 gives bright? No, wait!)
Bright, because reflection at both boundaries occurs at denser media, giving identical phase shifts of π and leaving path difference 0
questions.answer: Bright, because reflection at both boundaries occurs at denser media, giving identical phase shifts of π and leaving path difference 0
questions.correct_option: Bright, because reflection at both boundaries occurs at denser media, giving identical phase shifts of π and leaving path difference 0
questions.explanation: Here µ_lens (1.52) < µ_liq (1.65) < µ_plate (1.70). Both reflections occur at rarer-to-denser boundaries, so both experience a π phase shift. The relative phase difference is π - π = 0! At t = 0, Δ = 0 (constructive interference = bright central spot!).

questions.question: What happens to the central spot if the liquid film has an intermediate index: µ_lens (1.60) > µ_liq (1.45) > µ_plate (1.35)?
options: Bright, because neither reflection experiences a phase shift (both denser to rarer)
questions.answer: Bright, because neither reflection experiences a phase shift (both denser to rarer)
questions.correct_option: Bright, because neither reflection experiences a phase shift (both denser to rarer)
questions.explanation: Since µ_lens > µ_liq > µ_plate, both reflections occur at denser-to-rarer boundaries; neither experiences a π phase shift. At t = 0, optical path difference is zero, so the central spot is bright.

questions.question: Under what refractive index condition is the central spot of Newton's rings dark in reflected light?
options: When exactly one reflection occurs at a denser boundary while the other occurs at a rarer boundary (e.g. glass-air-glass: 1.5 > 1.0 < 1.5)
questions.answer: When exactly one reflection occurs at a denser boundary while the other occurs at a rarer boundary (e.g. glass-air-glass: 1.5 > 1.0 < 1.5)
questions.correct_option: When exactly one reflection occurs at a denser boundary while the other occurs at a rarer boundary (e.g. glass-air-glass: 1.5 > 1.0 < 1.5)
questions.explanation: A dark center requires an odd relative phase shift of π, which occurs if and only if one reflection has a π shift and the other has 0 (i.e. µ1 > µ_film < µ2).

questions.question: If a student measures the diameters of 20 rings on both left and right sides of the center, why is D_n calculated as |x_right - x_left|?
options: It directly measures the diameter across the center without needing to know the exact coordinate of the central spot
It doubles the magnification of the microscope
questions.answer: It directly measures the diameter across the center without needing to know the exact coordinate of the central spot
questions.correct_option: It directly measures the diameter across the center without needing to know the exact coordinate of the central spot
questions.explanation: Measuring from the left edge x_L to the right edge x_R directly yields diameter D = x_R - x_L, avoiding the uncertainty of locating the exact geometric center.
